name: Gonadorelin
summary: A lab-made copy of the brain hormone GnRH, which tells the pituitary to release LH and FSH; men take it to support testicular function, with little evidence.
what_it_is: Gonadorelin is a synthetic version of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), a 10-amino-acid hormone from the hypothalamus that tells the pituitary gland to release LH and, to a lesser degree, FSH, which drive the testes and ovaries. The body releases GnRH in pulses, and the pulse pattern is what keeps the system working; gonadorelin lasts only minutes in the blood. In medicine it has been used to test pituitary function and, given in pulses by a pump, to start ovulation or sperm production in people who make too little GnRH.

evidence.why: Pump-delivered pulses restore sperm production in men with congenital GnRH deficiency about as well as gonadotropin injections, in mostly observational studies; we found no studies of the way most men use it, alongside testosterone therapy.

status_us.label: No US product; pharmacies may compound it
status_us.note: Its US brand, Factrel, has been discontinued, but FDA identifies gonadorelin acetate as a component of an FDA-approved drug, and federal rules let licensed pharmacies compound with such ingredients on a prescription; for outsourcing facilities it is in Category 1 (under evaluation). WADA bans it for male athletes.

benefits.claim: Sperm production in men with congenital GnRH deficiency when given in pulses by a pump, about as often as with gonadotropin injections and about 5 months sooner, with larger testes, in mostly observational studies of 420 men
Sperm induced in 82% of 56 men with congenital GnRH deficiency treated with pulsed GnRH, versus 76% of 99 treated with hCG and hMG, in a single-center study

risks.risk: Allergic reactions, including hives and skin hardening at the injection site with repeated use; trouble breathing, ongoing flushing or a racing heart needs urgent care
Brief flushing, headache, lightheadedness, nausea or stomach discomfort
It acts only briefly and the body's response depends on pulse timing, so it is unclear whether occasional injections reproduce the effects seen with pump therapy
In people with a rare GnRH-secreting pituitary tumor, use may cause pituitary problems and sudden blindness
Repeated use may raise sex hormones and worsen hormone-dependent tumors

avoid_if: Hormone-dependent cancer, such as prostate or breast cancer (it may worsen)
Male athletes subject to anti-doping rules (banned by WADA)

before: Semen analysis if fertility is the goal
during: LH, FSH and testosterone or estradiol
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for off-label use; in fertility treatment, studies track these hormones and sperm production to judge response.

studies.title: Spermatogenesis of Male Patients with Congenital Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism Receiving Pulsatile Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Therapy Versus Gonadotropin Therapy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
studies.people: 420 men with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in 7 comparative studies
studies.finding: Pulsed GnRH and gonadotropin therapy produced sperm in similar shares of men, but GnRH did so about 5 months sooner and with larger testes. Allergic reactions occurred mostly with GnRH; breast growth and acne were more common with gonadotropins. The authors call for randomized trials.

studies.title: Comparison of outcomes between pulsatile gonadotropin releasing hormone and combined gonadotropin therapy of spermatogenesis in patients with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
studies.people: 155 men with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (56 on pulsed GnRH, 99 on hCG/hMG)
studies.finding: Sperm induction succeeded in 82.1% with pulsed GnRH and 75.8% with hCG/hMG, not a significant difference; GnRH worked about 2 months faster and produced larger testes, and its users reported no significant side effects.

ask_your_clinician: Why is my testosterone or fertility low, and which approved fertility treatments fit my situation?
If I am on testosterone, is there any evidence that gonadorelin injections keep my testes working?
Which hormone tests and semen analyses should we track, and how often?

notes_for_editor: Status combines three sources: Drugs.com (multi-source consumer monograph) says the drug is discontinued in the US with Factrel as the US brand; FDA's 503B list (March 21, 2025) marks gonadorelin acetate as a component of an FDA-approved drug and places it in 503B Category 1; FDA's 503A page allows ingredients of FDA-approved drugs. The compounding statement is an inference from these, and the original Factrel and Lutrepulse approvals were not checked on Drugs@FDA. Gonadorelin is not on FDA's 503A nominations list (May 14, 2026) or its Category 2 page. One targeted search found no human study of gonadorelin used alongside testosterone therapy; results were about hCG, so that use rests on anecdote. The pump-therapy evidence is mostly observational. Drugs.com also lists hundreds of heart-rhythm (QT) drug cautions that look generic to the GnRH drug class; omitted. Source 7 was read through a Spanish public-health library proxy of the BMC PDF. DrugBank also lists veterinary approval (not covered). WADA's ban applies to males (S2.2.1).
